title: IPO・マーケット監視ボード

items.title:
Anthropic has filed for an IPO, with its prospectus revealing just how fast the company is scaling.
FY25 revenue jumped 1,088% YoY to $4.59B, while compute and infrastructure spending rose 190% to $7.33B.
The company posted an $8.06B operating loss and ended 2025 with $20.28B in cash and short-term investments.
Anthropic’s two largest direct customers accounted for 24% of total revenue combined.
items.title_ja:
Anthropic は IPO を申請しており、その目論見書により同社がいかに急速に拡大しているかが明らかになりました。
25 年度の収益は前年比 1,088% 増の 45 億 9000 万ドルとなり、コンピューティングとインフラストラクチャへの支出は 190% 増の 73 億 3000 万ドルとなりました。
同社は80億6000万ドルの営業損失を計上し、2025年終了時点では202億8000万ドルの現金と短期投資を残した。
Anthropic の 2 つの最大の直接顧客は、合計収益の 24% を占めました。

items.title:
Music catalog buyer Duetti has lined up $665 million of new financing to buy more music catalogs from independent artists, according to the company.
The package is debt rather than equity: a $450 million asset-backed securitization anchored by Carlyle, $165 million of additional credit capacity from Viola Credit and a $50 million side facility.
items.title_ja:
同社によると、音楽カタログのバイヤーであるデュエッティ社は、独立系アーティストからより多くの音楽カタログを購入するために、新たに6億6,500万ドルの資金調達を計画しているという。
このパッケージは株式ではなく負債であり、カーライルを核とする4億5,000万ドルの資産担保証券化、ヴィオラ・クレジットからの1億6,500万ドルの追加信用枠、そして5,000万ドルの付帯設備である。

items.title:
Misr Life Insurance plans to list on the Egyptian Exchange, according to a company announcement.
Misr Insurance Holding, which is wholly owned by Egypt's sovereign fund, will sell 750 million existing shares, or 15% of the life insurer. The deal combines a private placement with qualified investors in Egypt and abroad and a public offering in Egypt.
Subscription and the start of trading are expected in December. EFG Hermes is sole global coordinator and bookrunner.
The sovereign fund had said in May that it would sell up to 20%.
items.title_ja:
同社の発表によると、ミスル生命保険はエジプト取引所への上場を計画している。
エジプト政府系ファンドが全額出資するミスル・インシュアランス・ホールディングは、生命保険会社の１５％に相当する７億５０００万株の既存株を売却する。この取引は、エジプト国内外の適格投資家との私募とエジプトでの公募を組み合わせたものである。
申し込みと取引開始は12月に予定されている。 EFG エルメスは唯一のグローバル コーディネーターおよびブックランナーです。
ソブリンファンドは５月、最大２０％売却すると発表していた。

items.title:
KKR has emerged as the preferred bidder for Ichibanya, the company behind Japan's CoCo Ichibanya curry chain, according to Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter.
House Foods owns 51% of Ichibanya. Both companies confirmed in August that they were considering all options, including taking the curry chain private.
Ichibanya shares rose about 2.6% in Tokyo on Tuesday to ¥1,135.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグが事情に詳しい関係者の話として伝えたところによると、KKRが日本のカレーチェーン「CoCo壱番屋」を運営する壱番屋の優先入札者として浮上したという。
House Foods owns 51% of Ichibanya.両社は8月、カレーチェーンの非公開化を含むあらゆる選択肢を検討していることを認めた。
壱番屋株は火曜日、東京市場で約２．６％上昇し１１３５円となった。

items.title:
Finnish satellite company ICEYE has launched a €41-a-share cash offer for Italian rocket maker Avio, aiming to buy every share and delist it from the Milan exchange, according to Avio.
The price is about 20% above Monday's close of €34.10. Avio's shares had already risen about 18% since Nov. 6. Its board will now evaluate the offer.
ICEYE, which builds radar imaging satellites, was valued at about €10 billion in a June funding round led by General Atlantic. The offer comes through a vehicle it controls called Iris 2.
items.title_ja:
アヴィオによると、フィンランドの衛星会社ICEYEはイタリアのロケットメーカー、アヴィオに対し1株41ユーロの現金オファーを開始し、全株を買収してミラノ取引所から上場廃止することを目指している。
価格は月曜終値の３４．１０ユーロを約２０％上回っている。 Avioの株価は11月6日以来すでに約18％上昇しており、取締役会は今後この提案を評価する予定だ。
レーダー画像衛星を製造するICEYEは、ゼネラル・アトランティック主導による6月の資金調達ラウンドで約100億ユーロと評価された。このオファーは、Iris 2と呼ばれる同社が管理する車両を通じて行われます。

items.title:
Anthropic will record about $14.2 billion of stock-based compensation when its IPO is completed, according to its amended filing.
The charge covers employee restricted stock units that only vest once the listing takes effect, valued off the $74 midpoint of its price range. As of Sept. 30, the company put total unrecognized expense on its restricted stock units at $32.3 billion.
Grants made since September add about $3.5 billion more over roughly four years. For scale, Anthropic's third-quarter revenue was $17.0 billion.
The IPO is expected to price on Wednesday.
items.title_ja:
修正申告書によると、AnthropicはIPO完了時に約142億ドルの株式ベースの報酬を計上する予定だという。
この料金は、上場が発効した場合にのみ権利が確定する従業員制限株式単位を対象とし、価格帯の中間点である74ドル相当となります。 9月30日の時点で、同社は制限付き株式ユニットの未認識費用の総額を323億ドルと見積もっている。
9月以降に行われた助成金により、約4年間でさらに約35億ドルが追加される。規模としては、Anthropic の第 3 四半期の収益は 170 億ドルでした。
IPOの価格は水曜日に発表される予定だ。

items.title:
Anthropic has committed about $900.9 billion of future spending, almost all of it on compute and infrastructure, according to its amended IPO filing.
About $451.6 billion of that falls due before the end of 2030 and nearly all of the rest between 2031 and 2045. The total leaves out another $150 billion to $175 billion of arrangements that carry no fixed dollar amount.
Roughly $186.2 billion can still be terminated, or depends on conditions such as a counterparty securing financing, sites or regulatory approval.
In the third quarter Anthropic brought in $1.72 of revenue for every dollar of compute and infrastructure expense, down from $2.08 in the second, which it puts down to buying pricier short-term compute. It is expected to price its IPO on Wednesday.
items.title_ja:
修正されたIPO申請書によると、Anthropicは今後約9,009億ドルの支出を約束しており、そのほぼ全額がコンピューティングとインフラストラクチャに当てられている。
このうち約4,516億ドルは2030年末までに期限が到来し、残りのほぼすべては2031年から2045年までに支払われる。総額には、金額が固定されていない協定の1,500億ドルから1,750億ドルが含まれていない。
およそ 1,862 億ドルは依然として契約解除される可能性があり、それは取引相手の資金調達、用地、規制当局の承認などの条件次第です。
第 3 四半期の Anthropic の収益は、コンピューティングとインフラストラクチャの支出 1 ドルあたり 1.72 ドルで、第 2 四半期の 2.08 ドルから減少しました。これは、より高価な短期コンピューティングの購入によるものだと考えています。水曜日にはIPOの価格が発表される予定だ。

items.title:
Hong Kong's two big AI listings from January have given back most of their gains, according to market data.
Zhipu priced its IPO at HK$116.20 and closed at a record HK$2,410 in June. It now trades around HK$347, about 86% below that peak, though still roughly three times its IPO price.
MiniMax priced at HK$165 and peaked at HK$1,238 in March. At about HK$122 it is roughly 90% below that high and 26% under its IPO price, after closing on Monday at its lowest level since listing.
Chip fears are hitting China's AI model makers, Bloomberg reports.
items.title_ja:
市場データによると、香港では1月からの2つの大規模AI上場が利益のほとんどを還元した。
Zhipu の IPO 価格は 116.20 香港ドルで、6 月には過去最高の 2,410 香港ドルで取引を終了しました。現在の取引価格は347香港ドル前後で、ピーク時より約86％低いが、それでもIPO価格の約3倍だ。
MiniMaxの価格は165香港ドルで、3月の最高値は1,238香港ドルとなった。約122香港ドルで、上場以来最低水準で月曜に取引を終えた後、その高値を約90％下回り、IPO価格を26％下回っている。
チップへの懸念が中国のAIモデルメーカーを襲っているとブルームバーグが報じた。

items.title:
India's central bank has told Tata Sons in writing to comply with its rules for the biggest non-bank lenders, including the requirement to list its shares, according to a letter reported by Reuters and Mint.
The letter is dated Nov. 16 and answers an Oct. 6 request from Tata Sons for guidance. It sets no new deadline.
The Reserve Bank of India put Tata Sons in that top tier in September 2022, which gave it until Sept. 30, 2025 to go public. In September this year, after the RBI turned down its request for relief, the Tata Sons board decided to comply, over the objection of Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata.
Tata Trusts own about 66% of Tata Sons and oppose a listing. The directive is expected on the agenda of the Nov. 26 board meeting, per Mint.
items.title_ja:
ロイター通信と造幣局が報じた書簡によると、インド中央銀行はタタ・サンズに対し、株式上場の義務を含む最大手のノンバンク貸し手に対する規則に従うよう書面で伝えたという。
この書簡は11月16日付で、タタ・サンズからの10月6日の指導要請に答えている。新たな期限を設定することはありません。
インド準備銀行は2022年9月にタタ・サンズをそのトップティアに入れ、これにより上場期限は2025年9月30日までとなった。今年9月、RBIが救済要請を拒否した後、タタ・サンズの取締役会は、タタ・トラスト会長のノエル・タタ氏の反対を押し切って、従うことを決定した。
タタ・トラストはタタ・サンズの株式の約６６％を保有しており、上場に反対している。造幣局によると、この指令は11月26日の理事会の議題となる予定だ。

items.title:
CVC plans to walk away from its signed deal to buy Italian dessert ingredients maker IRCA from Advent International for nearly €3 billion, according to Reuters, following a Financial Times report.
CVC said a forensic analysis of the information it received in due diligence showed the deal is no longer viable, and that pulling out is in the best interests of its investors. It told Advent a few weeks ago that it intended to pull out, per the FT.
Advent rejected the move. It called the agreement binding, said it expects CVC to complete the deal and will take all appropriate steps to protect its rights.
CVC agreed to buy IRCA in June. The company employs more than 2,200 people across 19 plants in Europe, the U.S. and Vietnam, supplying pastry and ice-cream makers.
items.title_ja:
フィナンシャル・タイムズ紙の報道を受けてロイター通信が報じたところによると、CVCはイタリアのデザート材料メーカーIRCAをアドベント・インターナショナルから30億ユーロ近くで買収するという署名済みの契約を破棄する予定であるとのこと。
CVCは、デューデリジェンスで受け取った情報を法医学的に分析した結果、この取引はもはや実行不可能であることが判明し、撤退することが投資家の最大の利益になると述べた。 FT紙によると、同社は数週間前に撤退する意向をアドベントに伝えたという。
アドベントはこの動きを拒否した。同協定には拘束力があるとし、CVCが協定を完了することを期待しており、その権利を保護するためにあらゆる適切な措置を講じると述べた。
CVCは6月にIRCAの買収に合意した。同社はヨーロッパ、米国、ベトナムの 19 工場で 2,200 人以上を雇用し、ペストリーやアイスクリームメーカーに製品を供給しています。

items.title:
OpenAI's latest funding round was never part of the plan, according to CFO Sarah Friar. She said it started after a well-known publication reported OpenAI was raising money when it was not.
The report set off a wave of investor calls. OpenAI chose to move quickly, aiming to be in and out of the market in about six weeks and finished by the midterms. The round values the company at $1.25 trillion and comes on top of the $122 billion raise it closed in March.
Speaking at a Semafor event, Friar said Anthropic going public first is good for the industry and for OpenAI, and that OpenAI is not worried about being second.
She also said advertising has brought in more than $1 billion in under 200 days.
items.title_ja:
CFOのサラ・フライアー氏によると、OpenAIの最新の資金調達ラウンドは計画にはまったく含まれていなかったという。彼女は、OpenAIが資金を集めていないのに資金を集めていたと有名な出版物が報じたことから始まったと語った。
この報告書をきっかけに投資家からの問い合わせが殺到した。 OpenAI は迅速に行動することを選択し、約 6 週間で市場に出入りし、中間選挙までに完了することを目指しました。このラウンドでは同社の価値は1兆2500億ドルと評価され、3月に完了した1220億ドルの調達に上乗せされる。
Semaforのイベントで講演したFriar氏は、Anthropicが最初に上場することは業界とOpenAIにとって良いことであり、OpenAIが2位になることを心配していないと述べた。
同氏はまた、広告が200日以内に10億ドル以上の収益をもたらしたと述べた。

items.title:
Specialty insurer Core Specialty has filed for an IPO on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "CORE", according to an SEC filing.
The company is selling no shares. All of them come from existing holders, led by a SkyKnight and Dragoneer vehicle with 43%, Enstar with 20% and Aquiline with 8%.
Founded in 2020, it says it is now the fourth-largest pure-play specialty insurer in the U.S., with $4.8B of gross premiums written over the past 12 months.
Revenue fell 16% to $2.16B in the first nine months, on more crop business ceded to reinsurers and $105.3M of investment losses. Underwriting improved: the combined ratio dropped to 93.0% from 98.2%.
J.P. Morgan and Goldman Sachs are leading the deal.
items.title_ja:
SECへの提出書類によると、特殊保険会社コア・スペシャルティは「CORE」というシンボル名でニューヨーク証券取引所にIPOを申請した。
同社は株式を売却していません。これらはすべて既存の保有者によるもので、SkyKnight と Dragoneer ビークルが 43%、Enstar が 20%、Aquiline が 8% を占めています。
2020年に設立され、現在は米国で4番目に大きい純粋専門保険会社であり、過去12カ月で48億ドルの総保険料を支払ったという。
再保険会社に譲渡された農作物事業の増加と1億530万ドルの投資損失により、最初の9か月の収益は16%減の21億6000万ドルとなった。引受業務は改善し、コンバインド・レシオは 98.2% から 93.0% に低下しました。
JPモルガンとゴールドマン・サックスがこの取引を主導している。

items.title:
Canadians will be able to buy Anthropic in Canadian dollars from the first day it trades.
CIBC says it will list an Anthropic Canadian Depositary Receipt on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the ticker ANTH, with trading expected to begin on 19 November. That is the day Anthropic is expected to make its Nasdaq debut.
The receipt carries a built-in notional currency hedge and is sold at a fraction of the price of the underlying share, so the entry cost sits well below the $70 to $78 range on the US offering.
It takes CIBC's line-up to 146 depositary receipts across six countries. The prospectus supplement is filed on SEDAR+, per the bank.
items.title_ja:
カナダ人は取引初日からアンスロピックをカナダドルで購入できるようになる。
CIBCは、アンスロピック・カナダ預託証券をティッカーANTHでトロント証券取引所に上場し、11月19日に取引が開始される予定だと発表した。その日は、アンスロピックがナスダック市場にデビューすると予想されている日だ。
レシートには想定元本為替ヘッジが組み込まれており、原株価格の数分の一で販売されるため、エントリーコストは米国での売り出し価格の70ドルから78ドルの範囲を大幅に下回ります。
CIBC のラインナップは 6 か国にわたる 146 件の預託証券に及びます。銀行ごとに、目論見書の補足は SEDAR+ に提出されます。

items.title:
Brussels has cleared UniCredit's takeover of Commerzbank, with no conditions attached.
The European Commission was notified on 9 October and approved it in phase one, finding no competition concerns anywhere in the European Economic Area. Combined shares were moderate across most German banking services.
Trade finance was the one place it had to look twice. Both banks are significant in documentary credit instruments, letters of credit and guarantees, and the Commission satisfied itself that enough public, private, cooperative and international providers remain.
Competition commissioner Teresa Ribera called it "the biggest cross-border banking deal since the financial crisis", and said cross-border consolidation can help overcome national fragmentation.
That leaves politics rather than antitrust as the obstacle. Berlin has objected to the approach since 2024 and still holds about 12.7% of Commerzbank from the 2009 bailout. Chief executive Andrea Orcel told investors on 9 November that he expects the remaining approvals by late November.
Source: European Commission, 16 November
items.title_ja:
ブリュッセルはウニクレディトによるコメルツ銀行買収を無条件で承認した。
欧州委員会は10月9日に通知を受け、欧州経済領域のどこにも競争上の懸念はないと判断し、第1段階で承認した。ドイツのほとんどの銀行サービスの合計株価は中程度でした。
貿易金融は二度検討しなければならなかった唯一の場所でした。両銀行は書面信用商品、信用状、保証において重要であり、欧州委員会は十分な公的、民間、協同組合、国際的なプロバイダーが残っていると満足した。
競争委員のテレサ・リベラ氏は、これを「金融危機以来最大の国境を越えた銀行取引」と呼び、国境を越えた統合は国家の分断を克服するのに役立つ可能性があると述べた。
そうなると、独占禁止法ではなく政治が障害となる。ベルリンは２０２４年からこのアプローチに反対しており、２００９年の救済で得たコメルツ銀行の株式約１２．７％を今も保有している。アンドレア・オーセル最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は１１月９日、投資家に対し、残りの承認は１１月下旬までに完了すると予想していると語った。
出典: 欧州委員会、11 月 16 日

items.title:
Our Next Energy, a Michigan maker of lithium iron phosphate battery cells, is going public through Wen Acquisition Corp and will trade on Nasdaq as ONEE.
The deal carries a pro forma equity value of about $1 billion: $600 million of pre-money equity plus up to $400 million of gross proceeds. That $400 million is $300 million sitting in the SPAC trust, assuming no redemptions, and a $100 million PIPE of which $30 million is committed so far, by two strategic investors in steel and defence.
Against that, the company reports $40 million of cumulative revenue. It also has more than $200 million of binding multi-year contracts, with locomotive makers serving four Class I railroads and with five defence prime contractors.
It runs two plants in Michigan, and the pack line at Novi has 3 GWh of annual capacity. Both boards have approved and closing is expected in the first half of 2027. $WENN, per the companies.
items.title_ja:
ミシガン州のリン酸鉄リチウム電池セルのメーカーである Our Next Energy は、Wen Acquisition Corp を通じて株式を公開し、ONEE としてナスダックで取引される予定です。
この取引には約 10 億ドルの推定株式価値があり、これには 6 億ドルのプレマネー株式と最大 4 億ドルの総収益が含まれます。この 4 億ドルは、償還がないと仮定して SPAC 信託に保管されている 3 億ドルと、鉄鋼と防衛分野の 2 つの戦略的投資家によってこれまでに 3,000 万ドルがコミットされている 1 億ドルの PIPE です。
これに対して、同社は累計収益が 4,000 万ドルであると報告しています。また、機関車メーカーと 4 つのクラス I 鉄道にサービスを提供し、5 つの防衛元請負業者との間で、拘束力のある複数年契約を 2 億ドル以上結んでいます。
ミシガン州で 2 つの工場を運営しており、ノビのパックラインの年間生産能力は 3 GWh です。両取締役会は承認しており、クロージングは​​ 2027 年上半期に予定されています。両社によれば、$WENN。

想定仮条件は2,340〜2,590円で、平均の2,465円で計算すると時価総額は約3,813億円。
2026年のIPOでは時価総額、調達規模ともに最大の案件です。
新株の発行はなく、既存株主による売り出しのみです。売出株数はオーバーアロットメントを含めると約4,915万株、約1,211億円になります。
グローバル・オファリングで、主幹事は野村證券、SMBC日興証券、BofA証券、ゴールドマン・サックス証券です。
前身のワークスアプリケーションズが次世代製品「HUE」の開発失敗と顧客との訴訟で経営難に陥り、2019年8月に会社分割で切り出したHR事業をベインキャピタルが取得しました。取得額は約1,000億円とみられています。
2023年7月、ベインは新ファンドから再出資し、シンガポール政府系ファンドのGICとの共同保有に移行しました。
その後、2024年にサイダスを約66億円、2025年にエンバーポイントを約228億円で取得しました。エンバーポイントはベイン傘下からの取得です。現在の保有比率は、完全希薄化ベースでベイン56.78%、GIC39.88%です。
2025年12月期は、売上収益657億円（前期比21.9%増）、調整後EBITDAは305億円（同27.2%増）で、マージンは46%でした。2026年1〜9月期は、売上収益562億円（同18.0%増）、調整後EBITDA291億円（同23.0%増）で、マージンは52%まで上がっています。
一方、最終損益は1〜9月期で赤字です。借り換えに伴う手数料の一括費用化や、合併で税務上の繰越欠損金を一部引き継げなかったことが響きました。
顧客基盤の強さは際立っています。
・導入先：約1,200法人グループ
・年間解約率：1.0%
・NRR：112%
・契約10年以上の顧客：66%
・クラウド比率：2021年末の16.8%から2026年9月末に81.5%
大企業の給与計算は一度入れると替えにくく、クラウド移行による単価アップを着実に取り込んでいます。
2023年の再出資時の株主資本は約1,547億円、1株1,000円です。想定価格2,465円なら株式ベースで約2.5倍、約3.4年のIRRで30%前後と試算できます。
純有利子負債は約1,750億円で、時価総額に足した企業価値は約5,560億円で、直近12カ月の調整後EBITDA約359億円に対するEV/EBITDAは約15.5倍です。10月に報じられた「企業価値ベースで5,000億円超」になっています
ただし、今回売却するのは保有株の3割程度にとどまり、上場後もファンドが約3分の2を保有し続ける計算です。
リターンの大半は上場後の株価次第で、残りを段階的に売っていく形になります。
2019年取得分のベイン旧ファンドは、企業価値ベースで約1,000億円から約3,500億円へ約3.5倍にしていて、レバレッジを考えると、株式ベースのリターンはそれ以上です。

DDR5 DRAM prices are up nearly 900% in just 15 months, and I think people are seriously underestimating how significant this is for the memory industry.
Back in August 2025, a 16Gb DDR5 DRAM chip was trading at roughly $6.17. Today, that same chip is trading above $60, representing a staggering 877% increase. Even after pulling back slightly from its October peak, prices remain near record highs.
And the reason behind this massive increase comes down to supply and demand. Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron have been prioritizing production capacity for HBM and high margin server memory, particularly as hyperscalers continue expanding their AI infrastructure. The problem is that this leaves less capacity available for conventional DRAM, creating additional pressure on an already tight market. What's particularly interesting is what this means for profitability. Memory manufacturing has enormous fixed costs, so when selling prices increase this dramatically, incremental revenue can translate into substantially higher margins and cash flow. That's especially beneficial for companies like $MU, provided higher spot prices eventually translate into realized contract pricing.
But there's another side to this story. Higher memory prices also mean higher costs for server manufacturers, PC makers, and smartphone companies. Eventually, those costs either get passed on to consumers or start eating into margins. And if prices remain elevated for long enough, we could see customers reduce memory configurations or delay purchases.
The biggest question now is how sustainable these prices are. Memory has historically been one of the most cyclical industries in semiconductors, and eventually higher prices encourage more supply. We're already seeing some signs of spot-price momentum cooling.
I'm still bullish on $MU and the broader memory industry over the long term but I think the real opportunity comes down to how long this supply imbalance can persist before additional capacity starts catching up with demand. 彼はこれが来るのを見ていただろうか？本誌によると、ジェンセン・フアン氏とその妻は、辞任のおよそ 8 か月前の 3 月に、約 105 億ドル相当の NVIDIA 株約 6,000 万株を取り消し不能な家族信託に譲渡したという。さて、この話には続きがあります。この譲渡は、ジェンセン氏と妻が最初に約 5,100 万ドル相当の NVIDIA 株を信託に預けた 2016 年に遡る不動産計画戦略の一環でした。その後の 10 年間でこれらの株式は大幅に値上がりし、この構造により連邦相続税の対象となることなく数十億ドルの利益が彼の相続人に渡される可能性がありました。ジェンセン氏が実際に105億ドル相当の株式を売却したわけではないことを理解することも重要だ。彼は所有権を家族信託に移したため、これらの株式は依然として NVIDIA の株価にさらされているということになります。
しかし、ここに私が興味深いと思うことがあります。数十億ドルを信託に移してから 8 か月後、ジェンセン氏は CEO を辞任し、NVIDIA は経営陣の大規模な危機に直面し、株価は大きな打撃を受けました。そして正直に言うと、ジェンセンがこれが起こることを予見していた可能性を完全に排除するつもりはありません。私たちが話しているのは、NVIDIA の構築に数十年を費やし、社内の動向を事実上誰よりも理解し、テクノロジー業界全体との関係を築いた人物のことです。彼が何かを持っていた可能性は十分にある

Okay, but why do we STILL not have a clear answer on whether this woman was actually a Chinese spy?
This entire situation has resulted in Jensen Huang stepping down as CEO of NVIDIA, billions of dollars in shareholder value being wiped out and now Trump himself is saying he's not even sure whether the central espionage allegation is true.
The FBI is investigating, and the Justice Department has acknowledged that it hasn't reached a conclusion. I understand these investigations take time, especially when national security is involved, but the lack of clarity is becoming a serious problem.
If there was an actual national security threat, investors deserve to understand the implications. But if these allegations turn out to be unsubstantiated, then we have to question how a situation with so many unanswered questions contributed to the removal of one of the most consequential CEOs in modern technology. I'm not saying Jensen shouldn't face accountability for his personal decisions, but there is a massive difference between personal misconduct and knowingly compromising national security.
And right now, those two issues seem to be getting conflated.
Liquid (@liquidtrading)
JUST IN: Trump says he’s not sure “that woman” involved with Jensen Huang was a Chinese spy.

Tomorrow's $NVDA earnings call is the most important earnings calls we've had in the entire AI trade.
NVIDIA is expected to report roughly $109B in quarterly revenue, but what investors are really going to be watching is what management says about the future of AI infrastructure spending, financing, and the company's strategy following Jensen Huang's departure. Remember, NVIDIA announced partnerships with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR aimed at mobilizing over $500B in third party financing for AI infrastructure. This is incredibly important because NVIDIA has been helping create the financial infrastructure needed to support the enormous capital requirements of the AI industry.
And now investors want to know whether those arrangements will continue under new leadership. We're talking about hundreds of billions of dollars in capital commitments, long term infrastructure projects, and an ecosystem that increasingly depends on access to financing to sustain its growth. There's also the question of circular financing. How much of the demand we're seeing is being supported by NVIDIA's own investments and financial commitments, and how much is coming from customers generating sufficient cash flows to finance expansion independently?
Then there's the supply chain. Jensen spent decades building relationships with TSMC, memory suppliers, networking partners, and the broader ecosystem. Investors will want reassurance that NVIDIA can maintain those advantages while executing its Blackwell and Rubin roadmaps. And finally, there's the issue of hyperscaler demand. Microsoft, Amazon, Google, and Meta are spending enormous amounts on AI infrastructure. Any indication that orders are accelerating, slowing, or being pushed into future quarters could move the entire semiconductor industry.
This is why tomorrow matters so much. It's not just about whether NVIDIA beats revenue expectations by a few billion dollars. It's about whether the company can convince investors that the financial structures, supply chain relationships, and extraordinary demand supporting the AI infrastructure boom remain intact without Jensen at the helm.

That is roughly $610 billion of new annual revenue in just two years, and BofA says it is using MORE conservative price assumptions than TrendForce to get there.

Goldman Sachs is forecasting nearly $3.8T in AI infrastructure spending tied to NVIDIA, Broadcom, and AMD systems through 2028.
According to these estimates, NVIDIA alone could account for roughly $2.65 trillion in infrastructure spending between 2026 and 2028, compared to approximately $876 billion for Broadcom and $228 billion for AMD. NVIDIA is still expected to dominate the market, but Broadcom could see some of the fastest growth as hyperscalers increasingly develop their own custom AI chips. What's particularly interesting is the sheer amount of power these systems will require. Goldman projects NVIDIA-related deployments increasing from 14 gigawatts in 2026 to 22 gigawatts in 2028, while Broadcom related deployments could quadruple from 5 to 20 gigawatts. We're talking about enormous amounts of electricity, networking equipment, advanced packaging, HBM, cooling infrastructure, and data center capacity needed to support all of this.
But here's where things get interesting with Jensen Huang's departure. I genuinely believe Jensen was one of the most important people in the entire AI ecosystem, not just NVIDIA. He spent years building relationships with TSMC, memory manufacturers, hyperscalers, and governments, coordinating supply chains and convincing companies to invest billions into expanding capacity. Losing someone with that level of influence creates uncertainty, especially when the industry is preparing to deploy trillions of dollars in infrastructure. And then there's the financing situation. These projections assume companies can continue raising enormous amounts of capital to fund AI infrastructure, something that's already becoming more challenging as lenders scrutinize the economics of these projects. Jensen's departure could make things even more complicated in the short term, particularly when it comes to maintaining investor confidence and coordinating major infrastructure deals.
However, I don't believe NVIDIA suddenly loses its technological advantage because Jensen is gone. CUDA, its networking ecosystem, customer relationships, and years of engineering work aren't disappearing overnight. And more importantly, demand for AI compute isn't suddenly going away either. This is also why I remain bullish on companies like TSMC, Micron, Broadcom, and optical networking suppliers. Regardless of whether NVIDIA, AMD, or Google's custom chips capture more market share, somebody still needs to manufacture these chips, supply the memory, and build the networking infrastructure connecting everything together. And with Jensen gone, I think execution just became a much bigger question mark. Still bullish on the broader AI infrastructure trade. President Trump just made some VERY interesting comments about Jensen Huang potentially returning as CEO of $NVDA, and now he's even considering discussing NVIDIA with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
Trump said he "would not mind" seeing Jensen reinstated as CEO, adding that he believes Jensen has "learned a big lesson." He also mentioned that he had previously floated Apple's Tim Cook as a potential replacement, but made it clear that he wouldn't be opposed to Jensen returning. And now, according to Kalshi, prediction markets are pricing in just a 15% chance that Jensen Huang returns as NVIDIA's CEO.
This is a pretty significant development, especially considering everything that has happened with NVIDIA over the past few weeks. What I find particularly interesting is that Trump is essentially leaving the door open for Jensen to return despite everything that led to his departure in the first place. And the latest comments about potentially speaking with President Xi add another interesting dimension to this situation. We don't know exactly what Trump intends to discuss regarding NVIDIA, but the fact that he's considering bringing the company up directly with China's president shows just how important NVIDIA has become in the broader relationship between the United States and China.
We're talking about a company whose technology sits at the center of the global AI infrastructure buildout, and decisions surrounding NVIDIA have implications for both countries. I genuinely think people underestimate just how important Jensen was to the entire AI ecosystem. We're talking about someone who spent decades building relationships with TSMC, SK Hynix, Micron, hyperscalers, and governments around the world. His ability to coordinate supply chains, secure manufacturing capacity, and convince companies to invest billions into AI infrastructure isn't something NVIDIA can easily replace.
Having Jensen return would arguably restore a tremendous amount of confidence across the industry, especially given the uncertainty surrounding NVIDIA's leadership and future. However, Trump being comfortable with Jensen returning doesn't necessarily mean NVIDIA's board is willing to bring him back. That's an entirely different issue. For NVIDIA shareholders, I think these comments are encouraging. Trump isn't publicly opposing a potential comeback, and he's now considering discussing NVIDIA directly with Xi. Personally, I wouldn't completely rule out a return, even with Kalshi currently putting the odds at just 15%. Now the question is whether NVIDIA's board actually wants him back and whether these developments could change that calculation.

Most people assume tighter chip export rules on China would be bad for memory. Nomura thinks it is the opposite.
Nomura looked at the three bills in Congress that would restrict chip exports to China. Its conclusion is that the demand the industry loses would likely be SMALLER than the supply that gets constrained.
If Chinese memory makers like CXMT lose access to United States equipment and technology, the global market loses future supply faster than it loses customers.
That is why Nomura expects memory supply and demand to get even tighter over the medium to long term, which supports prices.
I think this is one of the most underrated angles in the memory trade right now. $MU $SKHY
Melvin (@MelvinInvests)
BREAKING: Congress is moving to tighten AI chip export restrictions following the $NVDA scandal, but I actually think this matters less than people realize.
According to the Financial Times, lawmakers from both parties are pushing legislation that would further restrict advanced AI chip exports and give Congress the ability to review or block sales previously approved by the Trump administration. But here’s the thing. I don’t think this changes much for NVIDIA in China because Beijing has already made its intentions pretty clear.
The Chinese government doesn’t want its AI industry dependent on American technology, especially NVIDIA. Instead, Beijing is actively pushing domestic alternatives like Huawei’s Ascend chips, with the goal of building a semiconductor ecosystem that can compete with NVIDIA both domestically and internationally. And we’re already seeing that transition happen. NVIDIA’s share of China’s data center AI chip market reportedly fell to just 34% in the first half of 2026 as domestic competitors gained ground.
Every additional restriction gives Chinese companies another incentive to invest in Huawei, develop software around its architecture, and reduce their reliance on NVIDIA’s CUDA ecosystem. Ironically, this is exactly what Jensen Huang warned about. By restricting NVIDIA’s ability to compete in China, Washington could end up accelerating the development of its biggest future competitor.
Does this mean NVIDIA is in trouble? Absolutely not. Demand outside China remains enormous, and Huawei still faces significant technological and manufacturing challenges. But longer term, I think we’re heading toward two competing AI semiconductor ecosystems, one dominated by American technology and another built around China’s domestic industry.

On market crashes like today, I'm reminded of a piece of advice I got from a CIO mentor that traded during the dotcom and 08 crashes and lived to tell the tale.
He said: "Treat investing the same way you treat life."
That's all. It has stuck with me for many years because after filling in the blanks, you're forced to become "better" in both portfolio management and life management. It's uncanny how correlated they are.
Strip either one down and you're left with the same raw materials: time and uncertainty.
Every investment gives up something certain today for something uncertain tomorrow. So does nearly everything that matters in life. Love, learning, raising a child, starting a new job. Anything.
Both reward patience, but only after testing it.
You can't generate performance without risking losses, the same way you can't love without risking grief.
But fundamentally, the first rule of portfolio and life management is survival.
You can come back from most losses, but not from the one that takes you out of the game.
It's always darkest before the dawn.

FUNDA (@FundaAI)
The news surrounding Jensen Huang hits hard, and it throws a major wildcard into the medium-to long-term outlook for the AI supply chain.
Reflecting on the past few years, $NVDA's exponential leaps in compute came down to a founder-led culture of relentless boundary-pushing and trial and error.
Whether moving into CoWoS packaging and high-stack HBM, or aggressively driving high-speed copper cabling, CPO, orthogonal backplanes, Q-glass substrates, full-rack liquid cooling, and HVDC power, Jensen was always willing to stomach early yield pain and product delays to test the limits of physics and manufacturing with every data center generation. For the supply chain, Nvidia’s radical innovation translated directly into tangible dollar-content expansion. Steeper technical and production barriers allowed component and manufacturing players to command meaningful pricing premiums and these are the fundamental driver behind the massive value creation and multiple re-rating across the supply chain over the past three years.
If the pace of hardware iteration turns more conservative without Jensen's leadership, it is an open question whether the supply chain will continue to benefit from spec-upgrade tailwinds.

The history books will be very kind to Jensen Huang.
Trillions in economic value created...all downstream from his visionary leadership decisions.
One decision was on CUDA.
Nvidia started funding it in ~2006 and kept funding it for years while it dragged margins. There was no AI market to justify the spend which led to huge skepticism on the Street.
His foresight will prove to be legendary.
The second was on Mellanox.
Paying $6.9B for a networking company in 2019 was viewed as a very odd move for Nvidia. In fact, I'd say that it's the deal that let Nvidia sell the whole rack instead of the chip which is where much of Nvidia's pricing power comes from today. Very few CEOs get a call like that right.
Absolute legend.

But any catalyst, like if Iran War ends, can also change sentiment in a heartbeat (since bearish positioning is overwhelming).
- It's also clear financing has been tightening, since OpenAI only managed to raise $11B of their original $30B target so far.
- Markets are reacting enthusiastically to companies like $TE doing a $100M ATM today (nuking valuations)
- Although the "guppy" sector is probably the most sensitive to financing + rate changes.
On bright side... Neoclouds like $NBIS or $IREN seem to be adjusting by getting 100% capex prepayments or 90% GPU prepayments from their counterparties.
What I'd argue though is lower aggregate capex does not apply uniformly in supply chains.
- Mid-high range lasers for NPO/CPO are still sold out, as seen with $LITE now starting negotiations for 2030 capacity.
- MLCCs are seeing further tightening as content usage goes up for AI servers
- ABF substrates to InP substrates not really going anywhere.
If content per system goes up 10X-15X, capacity expands at 2-3X Y/Y, and capex drops 28%.
And content is so cheap that you can triple order and screw over competitors with wafer supply...
I'm pretty confident you'll see acceleration upstream in bottlenecks from optical components to substrates despite potential aggregate capex dropping.
Another rant is:
-I keep seeing this argument that "low P/E is a warning for cyclical that's going to crash" but these are just clown takes
Nobody seems to analyze duration scenarios like capacity expansion vs. content changes vs. demand. to actually see how long those earnings last.
If everyone seems to be exiting DDR2 lines, there's probably going be more tightness in 2027 despite consume demand weakening, even if it looks like it's low P/E.
- Also for concerns about CPO "delays", the same components like lasers are used for NPO. You'll still see 150-200mW NPO lasers or ELS NPO using the same 300–400+ mW lasers as CPO.
We'll just see acceleration with NPO as a bridge if CPO gets delayed and higher range lasers likely to remain in a severe shortage.
- Feels like markets have also completely discredited the merit of take/pay price floor LTAs as well that companies like SK Hynix to Samsung have.
If contractual agreements hold up, memory players look very undervalued.
TLDR:
- I think it's important to model in capex decreasing to numbers like -30% in hypothetical downside sceanrios.
Given AI profitability, it's clearly not sustainable for hyperscalers to aggregately increase capex $500B or $1T+ Y/Y, and that's never been a case I've argued.
- This is also not the same thing as demand destruction that markets are overreacting to now (which haven't happened yet).
- We can see demand revisions for GPUs, ASICs, and heavier cost parts of the supply chain, while acceleration increases elsewhere.
The nuances market miss by indiscriminately selling everything is going to present compelling opportunities when the dust settles. I think in the end institutions are probably going to end up owning more of the same names retail discovered early on.
Anyway, I think it's a good idea to try and survive until more earnings comes out.

items.title:
SOME PERSONAL THOUGHTS AHEAD OF WEEKEND
I wanted to share a few thoughts heading into the weekend because at least for me this has been one of most mentally exhausting stretches I've experienced investing in growth stocks.
And honestly one of the things I've found most difficult has very little to do with market itself since it's how much mental real estate I apparently occupy in the minds of certain "gurus" on this platform whom I've never met, followed or even spoken to.
I started sharing my thoughts on X back in 2023 simply because I genuinely love investing and wanted somewhere to talk about market, share my research and connect with people who enjoyed it as much as I did and I never imagined that would turn into an account reaching 100 million impressions every month or that I'd eventually find myself appearing on national television every week.
I'm incredibly grateful because this platform accelerated my career at a relatively young age and opened doors that otherwise might have taken me many more years to reach but I'd be lying if I said spotlight wasn't intense since the larger my audience becomes and more visible I am the more I've realized that success also seems to attract resentment from people I've never interacted with or affected in any way possible.
Daniel has a phrase for this that I think captures it perfectly because "hating up" is absolutely real especially online where people seem more comfortable attacking someone who has become visible than examining why that person's success bothers them in the first place.
Like I've had people accuse me of taking an investment idea from them despite fact that I don't follow them and have never even seen their work while others take a disagreement over a particular thesis and turn it into a personal judgment about whether I know anything about investing.
What I find especially strange is that some of these individuals are in their 40s and 50s have been doing this for decades and still seem determined to tear down a 33 year old who is simply willing to publish his research, explain what he believes and put his own money behind those convictions (I've never asked anyone to agree with me or suggested that my way of investing is the only way to succeed).
And I think that last part is important because I do all of this under my real name and face, publicly disclose what I own through my subs service, share my position sizes and actual dollars I've invested and expose myself to scrutiny over every good decision and every mistake along the way.
There's absolutely nothing wrong with choosing to remain anonymous and I respect anyone who prefers to operate that way but theres just a different level of personal accountability when people know exactly who you are and watch you explain your thesis on camera and follow your positions in real time and wait for first opportunity to use a bad outcome against you... just remember being wrong privately costs you money but being wrong publicly can also cost you reputation, confidence and peace of mind which is something I don't think people fully appreciate until they've experienced it themselves.
None of this is to suggest that criticism should be off limits because disagreement is a huge part of investing but what I truly struggle to understand is why disagreement so often has to become personal... especially during periods like this when so many people are already dealing with painful drawdowns and questioning decisions they made with the best information available to them.
Markets eventually humble every single one of us regardless of how experienced we are or how much success we've had and anyone who stays in this long enough will eventually experience a thesis that breaks or a position they sized too aggressively or a drawdown that exposes a weakness in their process or a decision they wish they could take back so that's why I think showing people grace matters so much because you never know when you'll find yourself on the other side of that experience hoping others will extend you the same understanding.
And also just remember it cost absolutely nothing to root for people, respect the work they're putting in and recognize that someone can be wrong about an investment without deserving to be ridiculed for it and I genuinely wish more people on this platform understood that being publicly wrong doesn't erase courage it takes to stand behind your own convictions in the first place.
And to the people who've made rooting against me a hobby I genuinely hope you find the same energy for your own work that you've found for mine because if you're spending more time waiting for someone else to fail than building something of your own then maybe my portfolio isn't what needs your attention.
I'll be here next week, same name, same face, same conviction.
items.title_ja:
週末に向けての個人的な考え
少なくとも私にとって、これは成長株への投資で経験した中で最も精神的に疲れる作業の1つだったので、週末に向けていくつかの考えを共有したいと思いました。
そして正直に言うと、私が最も難しいと感じたことの1つは、市場自体とはほとんど関係がありません。それは、私が会ったことも、フォローしたことも、話したことさえない、このプラットフォーム上の特定の「達人」の心の中で私がどれだけの精神的領域を占めていると思われるかということだからです。
私が X についての考えを 2023 年に共有し始めたのは、単純に投資が心から好きで、市場について話したり、自分の研究を共有したり、同じように市場を楽しんでいる人々とつながる場所が欲しかったからです。それが毎月 1 億インプレッションに達するアカウントに成長したり、最終的には全国放送のテレビに毎週出演するようになるとは想像もしていませんでした。
このプラットフォームのおかげで、比較的若い年齢で私のキャリアが加速し、到達するまでにさらに何年もかかっていた可能性がある扉が開かれたので、非常に感謝しています。しかし、視聴者が増えて知名度が上がるほど、成功は、私がこれまで交流したことのない、あるいは何らかの影響を与えたことのない人たちからの怒りを引き寄せるようにも見えることに気づいたので、スポットライトが強くなかったと言ったら嘘になります。
ダニエルはこれについてのフレーズを持っていますが、これはそれを完璧に捉えていると思います。なぜなら、「憎しみ」は絶対に現実のもので、特にオンラインでは、人々は誰かを調べるよりも、目立つようになった人を攻撃する方が安心しているようです。

The U.S. Commerce and Justice Departments have released a detailed timeline of their Megaspeed investigation, confirming $NVDA stopped selling to the Singapore data-center company in June 2025, when it was placed on Nvidia's internal "no sell" list.
Here's what the joint statement reveals:
2024: Commerce opened an investigation after detecting suspicious activity suggesting possible diversion of sensitive U.S. semiconductors.
May 2025: Investigators requested Nvidia's records covering direct and indirect sales to Megaspeed.
June 2025: Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its internal "no sell" list.
June 2025: U.S. and Singaporean authorities conducted an on-site inspection of Megaspeed and interviewed its then-CEO, Alice Huang.
Afterward: The Justice Department took the lead in the criminal investigation.
The disclosure comes after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized Commerce for not placing Megaspeed on the U.S. trade blacklist, despite support from four federal agencies.
Importantly, Nvidia's internal "no sell" list is separate from the government's Entity List.
Source: U.S. Commerce and Justice Departments

共同声明で明らかになった内容は以下の通り。
2024年：商務省は、米国の機密半導体の転用の可能性を示唆する不審な活動を検知した後、調査を開始した。
2025 年 5 月: 捜査官は、Megaspeed への直接および間接販売をカバーする Nvidia の記録を要求しました。
2025 年 6 月: Nvidia は、Megaspeed を社内の「販売不可」リストに入れました。
2025年6月：米国とシンガポール当局がメガスピード社を立ち入り検査し、当時のCEOアリス・ファン氏に事情聴取した。
その後: 司法省が犯罪捜査の主導権を握った。
この開示は、スコット・ベッセント財務長官が、4つの連邦機関の支援にもかかわらず、メガスピードを米国の貿易ブラックリストに載せなかったとして商務省を批判した後に行われた。
重要なのは、NVIDIA の社内「販売禁止」リストは政府のエンティティ リストとは別のものであるということです。

THE DOW FELL 22.6% IN ONE DAY. IT IS STILL THE RECORD
October 19, 1987 is known as Black Monday.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished down 508 points, or 22.6%, per Federal Reserve History. It remains the largest one-day stock market decline in history.
The setup: by late August, the Dow had gained +44% in seven months. On Friday, October 16, it lost 4.6%.
It was global. In the most severe case, New Zealand's stock market fell 60%.
Then came the rebound. In just two trading sessions, the Dow gained back 288 points, or 57% of the Black Monday drop.
Less than two years later, US stock markets were above their old highs.
items.title_ja:
ダウは1日で22.6％下落しました。それはまだ記録です
1987 年 10 月 19 日はブラックマンデーとして知られています。
FRBの歴史によると、ダウ工業株30種平均は508ポイント（22.6％）下落して終了した。これは依然として史上最大の一日の株式市場の下落である。
設定: 8 月下旬までに、ダウ平均は 7 か月で +44% 上昇しました。 10月16日金曜日には4.6％下落した。
それは世界的なものでした。最も深刻なケースでは、ニュージーランドの株式市場が60％下落した。
その後、リバウンドが起こりました。わずか 2 回の取引セッションで、ダウ平均は 288 ポイント、またはブラックマンデーの下落分の 57% を取り戻しました。
それから 2 年も経たないうちに、米国株式市場はかつての高値を上回りました。

items.title:
In the end, the biggest risk to Nvidia was Jensen Huang himself, per Business Insider.
Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and spent 33 years building it into the world’s most valuable company and the backbone of the AI boom. He ran it his own way: about 60 executives reported directly to him, and he personally handled key relationships like the one with TSMC founder Morris Chang.
That made him Nvidia’s single point of failure. When reports of his affairs surfaced, including one with Alice Huang, a woman US officials suspect was recruited by Chinese intelligence, there was no clear successor. Harvard Business School’s David Yoffie noted that Nvidia never had a systematic succession process.
Huang resigned Nov 12. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, the board is searching for a permanent replacement, and Nvidia has lost about $1 trillion in market value since the scandal began.
items.title_ja:
Business Insider によると、最終的に Nvidia にとって最大のリスクはジェンスン・ファン自身でした。
Huang 氏は 1993 年に Nvidia を共同設立し、33 年を費やして Nvidia を世界で最も価値のある企業、そして AI ブームの屋台骨に育て上げました。彼は独自の方法で会社を運営しました。約 60 人の幹部が彼に直接報告し、TSMC 創設者モリス・チャンとのような重要な関係を個人的に処理しました。
それが彼を Nvidia の単一障害点にしました。中国諜報機関にスカウトされた米当局者容疑者の女性、アリス・ファン氏との関係を含め、同氏の不倫に関する報道が表面化したとき、明確な後継者はいなかった。ハーバード大学ビジネススクールのデビッド・ヨフィー氏は、NVIDIA には体系的な後継プロセスがなかったと指摘しました。
Huang氏は11月12日に辞任した。CFOのColette Kress氏が暫定CEOであり、取締役会は恒久的な後任を探しており、NVIDIAはスキャンダルが始まって以来、時価総額約1兆ドルを失った。
